meta.title: Infer parameter types from usage inserts JSDoc type at wrong location for arrow function
meta.fix_ref: microsoft/TypeScript#41561 (fix(41526): add JSDoc type annotations before parameters), 2946318df0, 2020-12-05; git tag --contains: first in v4.2-beta / v4.2.2
meta.build_notes: npm typescript@4.1.6 (2021-06-16) and typescript@4.2.2 (2021-02-23), both behind typescript-language-server@0.5.1 (the latest wrapper release before 4.2.2), started with the pinned tsserver.js; the reported TypeScript version is checked on every session. Wrapper 0.5.1 is installed with the dependencies of its release date (install_builds.wrapper_before). The wrapper logs no TypeScript version; the build check verifies that its tsserver child runs the pinned tsserver.js.
meta.notes: The suggestion TS7044 (parameter implicitly any, a better type may be inferred from usage) stays after the misplaced JSDoc, as the report says. The era wrapper returns quick fixes as bare commands (_typescript.applyWorkspaceEdit) without a code-action kind, so the edit spec selects by title only.

settings_note: The issue names no settings; the file has // @ts-check; no jsconfig.json, so tsserver uses an inferred project.

files.note: the file name is not given in the issue

repro.steps: Open index.js (// @ts-check). Run the 'Infer parameter types from usage' quick fix on name inside the function body. Reported: the JSDoc '@param {string} name' is inserted above the return statement, where it does not apply, so the suggestion stays; expected an inline '/** @type {string} */' on the arrow parameter. Probe: after the fix, a fresh session on the edited file must neither report the targeted suggestion TS7044 on name nor a new error.
